+# --- the predictions parser: ONE implementation, TWO callers -------------------
+#
+# `hive-score` reads an order's `## Predictions` section to score it; `hive-launch`

+# defect; a gate that calls the scorer's own parser cannot.
+#
+# THREE FIELDS ARE SCORED, NOT FOUR. The authoring protocol

+# author writes all four, but `- Named risks:` is read by no instrument: it is not

+# and in every operator-facing message, because the alternative — quietly starting
+# to score it — would be a change to the contents of a launch gate, which is the
+# operator's call and not the tooling's.

+# refusal so the fix is copy-pasteable rather than a doc lookup.
+predictions_labels() {  # predictions_labels  -> the four literal labels, indented
+  cat <<'LABELS'
+    - Expected effort: <range> — <this project's median × a justified multiplier>
+    - Expected questions: <count or range> — <named seams, or a designed round-trip>
+    - Expected review outcome: <clean | minor rework | rework> — <why>
+    - Named risks: <what could turn the shape of the work>
+LABELS
+}
+
+# Parse an order file's `## Predictions` section. Sets, in the caller's shell:
+#
+#   PRED_SECTION       "present" | "absent"   — the heading, not its contents
+#   PRED_BLOCK         the section's raw text (heading exclusive; may be empty)
+#   PRED_DECLARED      1 iff the block carries the protocol's declared-unpredicted
+#                      one-liner, else 0
+#   PRED_EFFORT_TXT    verbatim prediction slice, EMPTY when that label did not
+#   PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT parse. A no-match is the expected partial-prediction case,
+#   PRED_REVIEW_TXT    never an error.
+#   PRED_FIELDS        how many of the three scored labels parsed (0..3)
+#   PRED_MISSED        the names of those that did not, comma-separated (may be empty)
+#
+# Always returns 0: "did not parse" is data. What to DO about it is the caller's
+# (hive-score records it; hive-launch refuses on one specific shape of it).
+predictions_parse() {  # predictions_parse <order-file-path>   (a missing path parses as absent)
+  local file="${1:-}"
+  PRED_SECTION="absent"; PRED_BLOCK=""; PRED_DECLARED=0
+  PRED_EFFORT_TXT=""; PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT=""; PRED_REVIEW_TXT=""
+  PRED_FIELDS=0; PRED_MISSED=""
+  [ -n "$file" ] && [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
+
+  # One awk pass, from the `## Predictions` heading to the next heading of any
+  # level, exclusive. The presence flag is printed as the FIRST line rather than
+  # inferred from an empty body, because "no section" and "a section we could not
+  # read" are exactly the two cases this whole function exists to tell apart — and
+  # an empty string cannot express the difference.
+  local raw
+  raw=$(awk '
+    /^##[ \t]*Predictions[ \t]*$/ { seen = 1; inblock = 1; next }
+    inblock && /^#/                { inblock = 0 }
+    inblock                        { body = body $0 "\n" }
+    END { print (seen ? "present" : "absent"); printf "%s", body }
+  ' "$file")
+  PRED_SECTION=${raw%%$'\n'*}
+  case "$raw" in *$'\n'*) PRED_BLOCK=${raw#*$'\n'} ;; *) PRED_BLOCK="" ;; esac
+  [ "$PRED_SECTION" = "present" ] || return 0
+

+  # carry a second copy, which is the whole of scope item 2. The `|| true` guards
+  # are load-bearing under `set -o pipefail`: a no-match grep is the expected
+  # partial-prediction case, and without them it would abort the caller.
+  PRED_EFFORT_TXT=$( { printf '%s' "$PRED_BLOCK" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected effort:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9.–—-]*[[:space:]]*worker-hours?' \

+    | grep -oiE 'Expected questions:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9–—-]*' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected questions:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+  PRED_REVIEW_TXT=$( { printf '%s' "$PRED_BLOCK" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected review outcome:[[:space:]]*[^.]+' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected review outcome:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )

+  local -a missed=()
+  if [ -n "$PRED_EFFORT_TXT" ];    then PRED_FIELDS=$((PRED_FIELDS + 1)); else missed+=("effort"); fi
+  if [ -n "$PRED_QUESTIONS_TXT" ]; then PRED_FIELDS=$((PRED_FIELDS + 1)); else missed+=("questions"); fi
+  if [ -n "$PRED_REVIEW_TXT" ];    then PRED_FIELDS=$((PRED_FIELDS + 1)); else missed+=("review outcome"); fi

+  # fires on *unparseable*, never on a gap the operator chose: a false positive
+  # here costs one unpredicted order that the scorer records honestly anyway, and
+  # a false negative blocks a legitimate launch. Those costs are not symmetric.
